questions.prompt: What is the puck state at this freeze?
questions.explanation: The puck has owner null at centre ice, so possession is not established.

questions.prompt: Which two cues should YOU watch?

options.text: Whether F2 can support the new carrier

questions.explanation: Possession and support decide the second play; the label does not tell who will control the puck.
The support job follows possession and the actual carrier, not a preset faceoff outcome.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a neutral support space that leaves room for the centre contest.
questions.explanation: This point offers a lane above the contest without crowding either centre.

questions.prompt: Gold C2 gains clean control. What should update first?

options.text: YOU should scan the defensive route toward the left net
Hold the same navy second-play spot

questions.explanation: Gold possession changes the direction and job; re-read C2, F2, and the left-net route.

questions.prompt: How should uncertain possession change your support call?
questions.explanation: Wait for the centre who controls the puck, then support that carrier or recover against the other team. The faceoff freeze does not choose the job.

sourceChecks.scope: Fetched via WebFetch (text extraction failed on the raw PDF) then read directly with the Read tool, printed pages 17-19 (PDF pages 23-25), '10-and-Under' section. Printed page 18's 'TEAM PLAY / Offensive Concepts' explicitly lists '2-on-1 situations' and '1-on-1 situations', directly supporting exp26b-u11-021's two-on-one carry topic at this age band. The same pages list general Individual Hockey Skills, Body Contact and Defensive Concepts (gap control, protect center of ice, stick on puck, backchecking) but do NOT explicitly name faceoffs or loose-puck battles; exp26b-u11-022's use of this source is therefore only general age/team-play support (consistent with the scenario's own hedged 'use' note: 'Lists skill/team topics; Canadian adaptation and answers remain experimental'), not a direct topical match. US age categories (10-and-Under) do not establish Canadian playing rules; no rule claim is made from this source.
